Modal Sandboxes

Creating a vibecoding platform

October 2026github.com/nicolaslara/vibecoding-platform

Feature demo

What we'll build

Create an app, change it, undo a turn, fork it, and pick up where you left off.

# example session: open the link, then send prompts
$ uv run vibecode.py chat alice
> A cake shop called Le Petit Trianon.
> Give it a royal Versailles theme.
# takes back the last message
$ uv run vibecode.py undo alice
# bob gets a copy of alice's project
$ uv run vibecode.py fork alice bob
# the tab was closed and it slept: back by name, where it ended
$ uv run vibecode.py chat alice
github.com/nicolaslara/vibecoding-platform

The architecture

Ephemeral Sandboxes per user

A script on the laptop, with a chat prompt.It finds or starts a Sandbox named after the user.The Sandbox runs her app from a shared template. She opens it by a private link.Idle, it goes to sleep. Its filesystem is kept, and the next Sandbox wakes from it.Each message runs a coding agent once, inside the Sandbox.The agent calls the model. Modal adds the key to its requests, outside the Sandbox.A Snapshot is taken before every message. Undo and fork start a Sandbox from one.A stable URL that finds or wakes her Sandbox.

Chapter 0

Scaffolding: an interactive prompt

  import sys        def ask():      """A line from the user. An empty line, EOF or Ctrl-C ends the chat."""      try:          return input("> ")      except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):          print()          return ""        def chat(user):      """Read messages, one per line."""      while message := ask():          print(f"{user} said: {message}")        if __name__ == "__main__":      commands = {"chat": chat}      if len(sys.argv) < 3 or sys.argv[1] not in commands:          sys.exit(f"usage: vibecode.py {'|'.join(commands)} <user>")      try:          commands[sys.argv[1]](*sys.argv[2:])      except KeyboardInterrupt:          print("\nleft")
Ctrl-C, EOF or an empty line: leave quietly. This part never changes
Our main loop
one function per command

Chapter 1

Proxy token, Model Endpoint, Secret

Proxy token

The key for it. It works in its own workspace only, and must be let into the Environment.

Authorization: Bearer wk-….ws-…
docs: webhook proxy auth ↗

Model Endpoint

An open model served by Modal behind an OpenAI-compatible API. Billed per token; nothing to deploy or keep warm.

$ modal endpoint create --shared --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3
docs: shared endpoints ↗

Secret

Named, encrypted values. Attach the Secret to a container to expose them as environment variables.

$ modal secret create model-token AUTHORIZATION_BEARER=…
docs: secrets ↗

Chapter 2

Serve each user's app

Where we are

  • chat is a prompt on the laptop: it reads messages and repeats them.
  • A model answers on Modal, with our key in a Secret.
  • Nothing runs for the user yet: no app, and no place to run one.

What we'll build

  • A Sandbox per user, running their copy of the app.
  • It starts in seconds, from an image built once.
  • A private link for the user's browser, with no public port.
  • It goes to sleep when nobody is looking.

Chapter 2 · step 1 of 5

boot: a Sandbox for the user. chat runs a command in it

  import modal     APP = "vibecode"  # every user's Sandbox lives in this App
  def boot(user):      """A new Sandbox for the user."""      app = modal.App.lookup(APP, create_if_missing=True)      sandbox = modal.Sandbox.create(          app=app,          idle_timeout=30,  # it ends 30 s after the last activity          timeout=3600,  # and after an hour at most      )         print("new", user, sandbox.object_id)      return sandbox
  def chat(user):      """Read messages, one per line."""+     sandbox = boot(user)+     hello = sandbox.exec("echo", "hello from a Sandbox")  # a command, run inside it+     print(hello.stdout.read(), end="")
one App holds every user's Sandbox
Sandbox.create: a container, started nowdocs: sandboxes ↗
it ends when nobody uses itdocs: idle timeouts ↗
exec: a command inside it, and what it printeddocs: sandbox spawn ↗

Chapter 3

Let an agent change the app

Where we are

  • Each user has a Sandbox that serves the template, and a private link to it.
  • chat still repeats the messages: nothing reads them.
  • The model answers, but nothing in the Sandbox calls it.

What we'll build

  • A coding agent in the Sandbox, beside the app.
  • One run of it per message.
  • Its steps on the user's screen as it takes them.
  • A turn that finishes even when the user leaves.

Chapter 3 · step 2 of 3

One turn of the agent is one shell command

  # One turn of the agent, as a shell command: $0 is the message.  #   -c            continue the project's chat, so the agent remembers the earlier messages  #   < /dev/null   OpenCode waits for as long as its stdin is open  #   2>&1          OpenCode prints its steps on stderr and only its last message on stdout  AGENT = 'exec opencode run --auto -c -- "$0" < /dev/null 2>&1'
the agent remembers the conversation

Chapter 4

Keep the key away from the agent

Where we are

  • A message changes the app: the agent works.
  • The model key is in the agent's environment: one echo prints it.
  • The agent runs commands nobody reviewed, and can send what it reads anywhere.

What we'll build

  • The key never enters the Sandbox.
  • Modal adds it to the agent's requests to the model, outside.
  • The agent and its config stay as they are.

Chapter 5

Save the work

Where we are

  • A message changes the app, and the key stays outside the Sandbox.
  • The work lives in the Sandbox, and the Sandbox ends 30 s after the tab closes.
  • Nothing is kept: the next chat starts from the template.

What we'll build

  • When a Sandbox ends, its filesystem is kept.
  • The next one starts where the last one ended.
  • reset still means the template.

Chapter 5

Snapshot everything, or only the project?

Filesystem Snapshotwhat we build

Base and project, one Image.

  • Nothing to mount.
  • Kept by the Exit Snapshot.
  • A new base misses existing users.
  • No warm pool.

Directory Snapshot, mounted

One base. The project is mounted.

  • A new base reaches every user.
  • A warm pool is possible.
  • A mount at every start.
  • Not kept by the Exit Snapshot.
github.com/nicolaslara/vibecoding-platform

Chapter 6

Undo a message and fork a project

Where we are

  • The user's work survives the Sandbox.
  • The agent got it wrong: there is no way back.
  • Two people cannot start from the same project.

What we'll build

  • A Snapshot before every message, on record per user.
  • undo: restart the user's Sandbox from the state before the last message.
  • fork: start another user's Sandbox from a copy of the project.

  def undo(user):      """Take back the last message: the user's Sandbox starts again, from the state before it."""      turns = turns_of.get(user, [])      if not turns:          print("nothing to undo")          return         before = modal.Image.from_id(turns.pop())      sandbox = running(user)      if sandbox:          sandbox.terminate(wait=True)  # a message that is still running ends with it      sandbox = start(user, before)      turns_of[user] = turns      print("turn", len(turns))      print("open", preview(sandbox, user))

  def fork(user, other):      """Give another user a copy of this user's project as it is now, in a Sandbox of their own."""      now = boot(user).snapshot_filesystem()      reset(other)      turns_of[other] = turns_of.get(user, [])      sandbox = start(other, now)      print("open", preview(sandbox, other))

Chapter 7 · optional

Give each user an address

Where we are

  • The link changes every time the Sandbox wakes.
  • It carries a token: whoever sees the link holds the key to it.
  • Someone has to run chat to wake the Sandbox.

What we'll build

  • One address per user, the same after every sleep.
  • No token in it.
  • A visit is enough to wake the Sandbox.

          def sandbox_access():              """A connect token for the user's Sandbox, which is woken first when it sleeps."""              nonlocal access, checked              with lock:  # one wake at a time: the requests that waited find it running                  if time.time() - checked > 5:  # used a moment ago, so it is still up                      sandbox = vibecode.boot(user)                      access = sandbox.create_connect_token(user_metadata={"user": user})                      checked = time.time()                  return access

Step 2: hot reload

Websockets

Proxy the WebSocket connection for hot reload

      def link():          ⋯          @web.websocket("/{path:path}")          async def websocket(tab: WebSocket):              """Hot reload: a websocket from the tab to the dev server, passed both ways."""              access = await asyncio.to_thread(sandbox_access)              async with websockets.connect(                  behind(access, tab.url).replace("https://", "wss://"),                  subprotocols=tab.scope["subprotocols"],                  additional_headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {access.token}"},              ) as dev_server:                  await tab.accept(dev_server.subprotocol)                     async def to_the_tab():                      async for message in dev_server:                          await tab.send_text(message)                     async def to_the_dev_server():                      async for message in tab.iter_text():                          await dev_server.send(message)                     both = [asyncio.create_task(to_the_tab()), asyncio.create_task(to_the_dev_server())]                  await asyncio.wait(both, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
